name: Billing portal + activation links + search invisibility

pages.purpose: Redeem an emailed link, or request a new one
Server-decided price and the Pay button
Shows a captured payment, honestly empty until Phase 5/6
Live licence status from the existing /entitlement function

noindex_layers.layer_1_robots_txt: app/robots.ts (Metadata Files API) -> 'User-Agent: *  Disallow: /' — verified live
noindex_layers.layer_2_meta_tag: noindex, nofollow, noarchive, nocache on all 7 pages — verified live in served HTML
noindex_layers.layer_3_http_header: X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow via proxy.ts on EVERY route — verified on 200, 307 and 501 responses

rate_limiting.primary_db_backed: public.activation_requests — 3 per identifier/hour, 10 per IP/hour, enforced in /send-activation
rate_limiting.identifier_storage: peppered SHA-256, never the raw email or phone
rate_limiting.secondary_in_process: portal/lib/rate-limit.ts on /api/create-order (single-instance, honest about its scope)

gst.WARNING: PLACEHOLDER, NOT CONFIRMED BY AN ACCOUNTANT. 'inclusive' means Rs109 already contains GST; 'exclusive' would change the amount actually charged to Rs128.62. The export/zero-rating assumption for international sales is a SEPARATE unconfirmed question. Do not change portal/lib/gst.ts without an instruction citing the accountant.

razorpay: INTENTIONALLY STUBBED. /api/create-order returns HTTP 501 {"status":"not_yet_available"}. No real payment can be taken. Phase 5/6 replaces the handler body. /confirmation therefore correctly shows 'No completed purchase found yet' for every user — that is the true state of the database, not a bug and not faked data.

session_bridge.mechanism: custom 256-bit single-use token -> /verify-activation -> admin.generateLink({type:'magiclink'}) -> verifyOtp({token_hash, type:'email'}) -> httpOnly cookies
session_bridge.token_storage: SHA-256 hash only; a full dump of activation_tokens cannot produce a usable link
session_bridge.email_transport: direct HTTPS call to api.resend.com, not Supabase Auth SMTP

app_untouched.statement: The signup -> activation-email connection is made entirely server-side: auth.users INSERT -> handle_new_user() -> licences INSERT -> on_licence_created_send_activation trigger -> net.http_post -> /send-activation. Proven with a real throwaway signup.

deviations: middleware.ts -> proxy.ts. Next.js 16 renamed Middleware to Proxy and the installed docs mark middleware.js DEPRECATED. The X-Robots-Tag layer depends on this file loading, so the deprecated name was a real risk of silent failure.
robots.txt/route.ts -> app/robots.ts, the canonical Metadata Files API convention in the installed Next.js version.

ADDED explicit service_role grants to the migration. Verified against pg_default_acl that new tables here grant client roles only Dxtm — service_role gets NO SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE. Without the added grants both Edge Functions would have failed with 42501 on their first query, the same omission that already required three corrective migrations in Phases 1-3.

Database Webhook hand-rolled with pg_net + Vault. supabase_functions.http_request did not exist on this project and pg_net was not installed. The dashboard wizard stores the auth header as a literal in the trigger body, readable via pg_get_functiondef; reading it from Vault instead keeps the shared secret out of the catalog and out of git.

verifyOtp uses type:'email', not 'magiclink'. The installed SDK marks the magiclink verify type deprecated and documents token-hash redemption as {token_hash, type:'email'}. generateLink still uses type:'magiclink'.

ADDED app/api/activate/route.ts. A Next.js Server Component cannot write cookies, and setting the session cookie is the entire purpose of redeeming the token, so the redemption must live in a Route Handler. /activate?t= forwards to it. The redirect also strips the single-use token from the address bar.

ADDED small shared modules rather than duplicating constants across 10 files: lib/seo.ts (the one noindex definition), lib/theme.ts (the Mission Control palette), lib/entitlement.ts (the /entitlement caller), app/legal/layout.tsx (the DRAFT banner), plus two client components for the only two interactive controls (activate/request-form.tsx, checkout/pay-button.tsx).

DID NOT create portal/lib/supabase/client.ts. Session cookies are httpOnly by design (Step 6), which means a browser-side Supabase client cannot read the session. All four pages are server-rendered, so a browser client would have been non-functional dead code.
npm install pulled @supabase/supabase-js alongside @supabase/ssr — it is a required peer dependency of it, not an extra choice.
Dropped an `import 'server-only'` from lib/rate-limit.ts: the package is not installed and adding it exceeded the stated dependency budget. Replaced with a comment.

The per-IP rate limit trusts cf-connecting-ip / x-forwarded-for, which are spoofable until Cloudflare (Part D) sits in front and overwrites them. The per-identifier limit is the non-spoofable control.
open_items_for_owner: GST treatment (inclusive vs exclusive) and the 18% rate need accountant confirmation.
Whether international sales are zero-rated exports is a separate accountant question.
All three legal pages are DRAFTS and carry [CONFIRM] markers where a decision is needed (entity name, addresses, contact emails, retention periods, grievance officer).

PHONE-ONLY SIGNUPS CANNOT RECEIVE AN ACTIVATION EMAIL. A user who signs up with a mobile number and no email address has no address to send to; /send-activation reports 'no_email_on_profile' rather than pretending. An SMS activation path belongs with the MSG91 work in Phase 5/6.

Resend currently sends from onboarding@resend.dev and, until a domain is verified, only delivers to the Resend account owner's address. Set ACTIVATION_FROM_EMAIL and BILLING_DOMAIN once the real domain exists.
BILLING_DOMAIN is currently set to http://localhost:3000.
